summary: This case study presents a practical workaround for programmatically moving open macOS windows across Spaces while keeping System Integrity Protection (SIP) enabled, combining CGEvent mouse drag actions with System Events AppleScript shortcuts. The author provides clear code snippets, timing profiles, and explores the undocumented com.apple.spaces plist bindings for launch-time assignment.
strengths: Addresses a real-world developer limitation in macOS automation under SIP-on constraints
Provides clean, concrete Swift implementation snippets for hybrid HID and AppleScript event posting
Documents timing profiles and failure modes (e.g., event composition failures, focus stealing)
Explores the underlying com.apple.spaces plist structure and app-bindings
weaknesses: Relies on undocumented internal macOS plist keys and behavior which may break across minor OS updates
Linked repository is private, limiting full end-to-end code inspection without cloning locally
Window-move gesture depends heavily on user-enabled Mission Control keyboard shortcuts
suggestions: Publish a minimal public demonstration repository to aid reproducibility
Expand on error handling when Accessibility permissions are missing or revoked
Document how multi-display setups affect title bar coordinate calculation

claims.text: Yabai 7.1.5 requires System Integrity Protection off and a Dock scripting addition for full space control.
Default desktop membership lives in ~/Library/Preferences/com.apple.spaces.plist under app-bindings.
